headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks via RD-Agent’s browser/networked research outputs feeding Superset; no direct pairwise evidence, so uncertainty is elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can run browsers and has broad network egress, so it may ingest untrusted web content; Superset can consume API-driven inputs and render analytics. A direct bridge is not documented, but if RD-Agent outputs are copied into Superset dashboards or queries, prompt-like content could influence downstream interpretation. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF RD-Agent browser-scraped content is pasted into Superset descriptions, SQL, or dashboard metadata
IF Superset is configured to treat imported text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Use a manual review step before importing RD-Agent outputs into Superset
Strip instructions from scraped text before upload
Disable copy-paste of raw web content into operational fields
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and requests multiple API keys; Superset has allowlisted egress and can expose data through its API. If they share a workspace or operator account, sensitive RD-Agent material could flow into Superset outputs or external calls. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are run on the same shared workspace or account
IF RD-Agent artifacts containing reports, traces, or logs are imported into Superset
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials
Do not import logs or traces into Superset without redaction
Review outbound destinations on Superset before enabling connectors
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, while Superset exposes an API and can make allowlisted network calls. The profiles do not show shared write access, shared mutable storage, or overlapping OAuth scopes, so a direct conflict is not established. Any contention would require an external shared resource not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or database
IF an external orchestrator gives them overlapping write permissions
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same database
Use file locks or job queues
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent produces research outputs and logs; Superset is a downstream analytics tool that can render or operationalize imported data. If Superset treats RD-Agent outputs as authoritative without validation, errors can cascade into misleading dashboards or decisions. The interaction is plausible but undocumented, so medium is safer than low.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or datasets are populated directly from RD-Agent outputs
IF no validation or review step checks RD-Agent-generated facts before publication
mitigations: Add a human review gate before publishing outputs
Validate RD-Agent outputs against source data
Mark imported datasets as provisional
Limit automated refreshes until checks pass
requires-engineering: implement schema and freshness validation

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports and logs and requests several API keys, while Superset’s profile shows no special residency or certification claims. No concrete mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance risk is supportable. The other agent is not cited beyond its generic open-source profile because no specific residency constraint is present.
conditions: IF regulated financial reports or logs are uploaded into a Superset deployment with stricter residency or retention rules
IF the deployment stores imported data outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Classify data before import
Avoid uploading regulated records to Superset
Check retention settings on both systems
Document the data flow for compliance review
